:
The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

sentences.text:
2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 26.04.2023 at about 11.20 a.m. P.Aswathamma was crossing the BB Road,
near Sanjeevini Nagara Cross, Bengaluru, at that time, driver of Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6415 came in rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against hr, due to the impact, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, she was taken to Aster CMI Hospital, wherein Doctors declared as dead on the way to the hospital.

Thereafter post mortem was conducted at Yelahanka Government Hospital,
SCCH 5 petitioners have shifted the body to their native Andhra Pradesh and performed funeral and obsequies ceremony by spending more than Rs.2,00,000/-.
3. At the time of accident, deceased/P.Aswathamma was aged about 82 years, working as coolie-cum-agriculturist, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

petitioner No.1 is son, petitioner No.2 and are daughters of the deceased, due to sudden death of the deceased, petitioners life has became dark,miserable, depressed and put to great financial hardship.
Out of the said accident, crime No.95/2023 is registered against the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6415 before Hanumantha Reddy vs Thimmarayappa.

M on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163793961/
2 the Hebbal Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said Eicher Canter, they are jointly and SCCH 5 severally liable to pay compensation.
So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared through his advocate and filed written statement and denied entire averments of the petition with regard to age, occupation of the deceased.
Respondent No.2 seeks protection available under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6415 does not possessed valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.

Further submitted issuance of policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of said Eicher SCCH 5 Vehicle and if there is any liability to pay the compensation, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased P.Ashwathamma died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 26.04.2023 at about 11.20 a.m. near B.B.Road,
Sanjeevini Nagara Cross, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6415 which caused the accident and dashed SCCH 5 against the deceased, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so how much and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
6. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.1/son of the deceased deposed his evidence as PW-1 and exhibited 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his evidence.

On the other hand,
respondents have not lead evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 SCCH 5 Hanumantha Reddy vs Thimmarayappa.M on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163793961/
3  ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:- In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/son of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief-examination he has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of MLC is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of crime details form is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of AIR Form is marked as Ex.P.8, copy of Inquest is marked as Ex.P.9, copy of P.M. Report is marked as Ex.P.10 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.11.
9.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records which were marked i.e., FIR, complaint, MLC,
crime details form, sketch, Sec.133 notice, reply, AIR SCCH 5 form, inquest, P.M.Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 26.04.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.
Per contra, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non- causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of P.Aswathamma out of the accident held on 26.04.2023 at about 11.20 a.m. while crossing BB Road,
near Sanjeevini Nagar, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
SCCH 5 11.
The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6415.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/P.Aswathamma was aged about 82 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, the notarized copy of aadhar card of deceased is marked as Ex.P.12, wherein year of birth 1941, the alleged accident was occurred in the year 2023.

Accordingly relying on aadhar card, age of the deceased is considered about 82 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 2 is SCCH 5 applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation and others i.e., as per para 21 of the Hon'ble Apex Court judgment, reduced by one unit for 5 years.
So here in this case, the age of the deceased is 82 years, hence said multiplier is taken into consideration.
13. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as coolie-cum-agriculturist, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
In this regard, petitioners have not produced any documents.

Under such Hanumantha Reddy vs Thimmarayappa.M on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163793961/
4 circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.15,250/- p.m. SCCH 5 14.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further petitioner No.1 is son, petitioners No.2 and 3 are daughters of the deceased P.Aswathamma.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar card of petitioner No.1 to 3 marked as Ex.P.12 it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased/P.Aswathamma, hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

15. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 2 to 3, then 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/3rd of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

16. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, there is no addition to be added to the monthly SCCH 5 income, if the deceased was aged above 60 years.

National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, deceased was aged about 82 years, hence question of adding future prospects to income does not arise.
17. Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

Sl. Particulars Calculation Total No.
 (i) Monthly Income Rs.15,250/-
(ii) 1/3rd of (ii) of the Rs.15,250/- (-) same to be deducted Rs.5,083/- = towards personal and living expenses Monthly income Rs.10,167/-

(iii) Compensation after Rs.10,167/- x Rs.2,44,008/-
multiplier of 2 is 12 x 2 applied 18.
Further petitioner No.1 being the son, petitioner No.2 being the daughter the deceased are entitled for Rs.30,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium.
SCCH 5
Further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

19. The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 2,44,008-00 Hanumantha Reddy vs Thimmarayappa.M on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163793961/
5 2. Loss of parental consortium 90,000-00 (Rs.30,000/- each to Petitioner No.1 to 3)

This amount is taken into consideration as per the ruling of petitioner's counsel rendered by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.101724/17 in between Smt.Santa and others V/s.
Sri.Avinash.
3. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 4.
Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 Total 3,64,008-00 20.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,64,008/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH 5 21.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.USGI/POSWEB/0911804/00/000 which is valid for the period from 03.01.2023 to 02.01.2024,
the alleged accident was occurred on 26.04.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Further there is no dispute about the existence of policy.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH 5 ::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,64,008/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Sixty Four Thousand Eight Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 40:30:30 in the award amount.
The petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and Hanumantha Reddy vs Thimmarayappa.

6
remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.

Draw award accordingly.
